aliases: rcog ovarian cysts in postmenopausal women

inputs.label: Postmenopausal
inputs.how_stated: true when the clinical details or dictation state the woman is postmenopausal (postmenopausal bleeding counts); false when she is stated to be premenopausal. Age alone does not settle it.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope

inputs.label: Ovarian malignancy already confirmed
inputs.how_stated: true only when this ovarian mass is already confirmed as ovarian cancer (histology or cytology); false when it is undiagnosed. A mass merely suspected of malignancy on imaging is false.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope: management of confirmed ovarian malignancy is outside the remit

inputs.label: Cyst morphology on ultrasound
inputs.how_stated: simple: round or oval, thin or imperceptible wall, posterior acoustic enhancement, anechoic fluid, no septations or nodules. unilocular_non_simple: one locule, no solid areas, but not all simple features (e.g. echogenic contents, thick wall, incomplete septum). multilocular: complete septation, no solid areas. solid_areas: solid areas (solid nodules, papillary projections or solid component) without complete septation, including mainly solid masses. multilocular_solid: complete septation and solid areas.

locator.section: 4.4.1: simple cyst (five features) and complex cyst (septation, solid nodules, papillary projections)

inputs.label: Bilateral lesions
inputs.how_stated: true when both ovaries have a cyst or mass; false when the other ovary is normal or not involved. A contralateral simple, unilocular cyst of 3 cm or less does not count (RCOG: not clinically significant).

locator.section: 5.1.1 Calculation of the RMI I: bilateral lesions

inputs.label: Ascites
inputs.how_stated: true when ascites is reported on this scan; false when no ascites or no free fluid is reported

locator.section: 5.1.1 Calculation of the RMI I: ascites

inputs.label: Metastases on imaging
inputs.how_stated: true when the imaging shows metastatic disease (e.g. peritoneal or omental deposits, liver metastases); false when none is described

locator.section: 5.1.1 Calculation of the RMI I: metastases

inputs.label: Cyst maximum diameter
inputs.how_stated: maximum diameter of the cyst in centimetres (millimetres convert), e.g. '4.2 cm simple cyst' or '42 x 30 mm'; for bilateral cysts, the larger

locator.section: 6.1.1: cysts of 3 cm or less; more than 3 cm but less than or equal to 5 cm

inputs.label: Symptomatic
inputs.how_stated: true when the woman has symptoms attributed to the cyst or adnexa, or persistent or frequent symptoms suggesting ovarian cancer (e.g. persistent abdominal distension, feeling full or loss of appetite, pelvic or abdominal pain, urinary urgency or frequency); false when the cyst is incidental and she is asymptomatic. The scan indication alone (e.g. 'abdominal pain') is not enough.

outcomes.classification: Simple, unilateral, unilocular ovarian cyst of 3 cm or less in an asymptomatic postmenopausal woman: low risk of malignancy.
caveats: RCOG regards such cysts as clinically inconsequential; whether to mention them in the report is at the reporting clinician's discretion.
With ascites or metastases the CT and MDT route applies instead (library routing; RCOG's 3 cm statement does not address them).

locator.section: 6.1.1 (December 2025 update); Clinical algorithm p6; Section 2 p7

outcomes.classification: Postmenopausal ovarian cyst with RMI I of 200 or more, or with ascites or metastases on imaging: increased risk of malignancy.
outcomes.recommendation: CT abdomen and pelvis, and referral to the gynaecological oncology MDT.
caveats: With ascites or metastases this route applies whatever the RMI I, as malignancy is suspected from the ultrasound findings (library routing of RCOG's text).
Further surgery (staging laparotomy or pelvic clearance) and its setting follow the MDT's view of how likely malignancy is.
Some centres use an RMI I threshold of 250 in local protocols; RCOG's pathway uses 200.
RMI I is a triage tool: benign conditions can raise it and early cancer may not.

locator.section: 5.1 Which RMI should be used?; 4.4.3.1 p14; Clinical algorithm p6

outcomes.classification: Postmenopausal ovarian cyst, RMI I under 200 (low risk), with a feature excluding conservative management: symptoms, non-simple features, over 5 cm, multilocular or bilateral.
caveats: RCOG: women with RMI I under 200 are suitable for laparoscopic management, unless the clinical picture, ultrasound or tumour markers suggest malignancy; then CT abdomen and pelvis with gynaecological oncology MDT referral.
RCOG advises discussing the pros and cons of conservative versus surgical management at RMI I under 200.
MRI is the second-line test when ultrasound is inconclusive for an indeterminate cyst.
Where surgical risk is high, repeat imaging is often safer than immediate surgery.

locator.table: Clinical algorithm: RMI I < 200, ANY box, consider surgery salpingo-oophorectomy (usually bilateral)

outcomes.classification: Asymptomatic simple, unilateral, unilocular ovarian cyst over 3 cm and up to 5 cm with normal CA125: low risk of malignancy.
outcomes.recommendation: Consider conservative management: repeat CA125 and transvaginal ultrasound in 4-6 months.
caveats: If resolved at repeat: discharge. If unchanged: repeat in another 4-6 months, then individualise treatment after discussion with the woman. If features change: consider intervention.
Discharge after 1 year is reasonable if the cyst is unchanged or smaller with normal CA125, considering the woman's wishes and surgical fitness.
Normal CA125 is read here as 35 iu/ml or less, the routinely used cut-off (library reading).

locator.section: 6.1.1; Clinical algorithm p6: consider conservative management, repeat assessment in 4-6 months

outcomes.classification: Simple, unilateral, unilocular ovarian cyst of 3 cm or less in a symptomatic postmenopausal woman.
caveats: RCOG regards simple cysts of 3 cm or less as clinically inconsequential, so consider whether the symptoms are due to the cyst.
Symptomatic means symptoms from the cyst, or persistent or frequent symptoms suggesting ovarian cancer; the scan indication alone is not enough.

locator.section: 6.1.1: if a woman is symptomatic, further surgical evaluation is necessary; Section 2 p7

outcomes.classification: Asymptomatic simple, unilateral, unilocular cyst over 3 cm and up to 5 cm with raised CA125 (over 35 iu/ml): does not meet RCOG criteria for conservative management.
outcomes.recommendation: Offer surgical treatment, with the setting and surgeon guided by the RMI.
caveats: The RMI I is 0 here (ultrasound score 0) whatever the CA125, so the RMI does not flag this cyst; the conservative criteria require a normal CA125.
RCOG advises discussing the pros and cons of conservative versus surgical management in women at low risk (RMI I under 200).
CA125 is raised by benign conditions (e.g. endometriosis, fibroids, peritoneal irritation) and should not be used alone to decide if a cyst is malignant.
The clinical algorithm lists the conservative criteria without CA125; the text requires a normal CA125 and is followed here.

locator.section: 6.1.2 What are the available surgical options?; 6.1.1 p19 (normal CA125 required)

outcomes.classification: RCOG GTG 34 does not apply: it covers ovarian cysts in postmenopausal women, not premenopausal women or confirmed ovarian malignancy.

locator.section: 1. Purpose and scope

summary.text: Every postmenopausal ovarian cyst is assessed with serum CA125 and transvaginal ultrasound (with transabdominal as needed), and the RMI I is calculated.
RMI I 200 or more: CT abdomen and pelvis and gynaecological oncology MDT referral. Under 200: low risk; a general gynaecologist may manage these women.

locator.section: 5.1 Which RMI should be used?

summary.text: Asymptomatic simple, unilateral, unilocular cysts: 3 cm or less need no follow-up (December 2025 update); over 3 cm up to 5 cm with normal CA125 may be managed conservatively with repeat assessment in 4-6 months.
Symptomatic women and cysts that are non-simple, over 5 cm, multilocular or bilateral (RMI I under 200): consider salpingo-oophorectomy, usually bilateral; laparoscopic management is suitable.

definitions.text: Simple cyst (transvaginal ultrasound): round or oval, thin or imperceptible wall, posterior acoustic enhancement, anechoic fluid, and no septations or nodules. It indicates a benign process in 95-99% of postmenopausal women.
Complex cyst: one or more of complete septation (multilocular cyst), solid nodules or papillary projections.

RMI I = U x M x CA125 (iu/ml). U: 1 point each for multilocular cyst, solid areas, metastases, ascites and bilateral lesions; U = 0 for 0 points, 1 for 1 point, 3 for 2-5 points. M = 3 for every postmenopausal woman.

locator.section: 5.1.1 Calculation of the RMI I

definitions.text: CA125: a routinely used cut-off is 35 iu/ml; lower levels (about 20 iu/ml) are found in healthy postmenopausal women. A normal value does not exclude ovarian cancer.

pitfalls.text: A cyst first seen on CT needs an ultrasound to calculate the RMI, unless the CT clearly shows ovarian malignancy with widespread intra-abdominal disease.
CT, MRI and PET-CT are not recommended for initial evaluation; MRI is second-line when ultrasound is inconclusive.
Some centres use an RMI I threshold of 250 (NICE); this entry uses RCOG's 200.
RCOG accepts the IOTA classification as an alternative to the RMI for experienced operators; any M-rule feature warrants gynaecological oncology referral. IOTA is not encoded in this pathway.
